# Recording infrastructure for your agent. (https://toru.tools/)
Your coding agent records your product demos itself: launch clips, changelog GIFs, help-center guides and bug repros. Toru is its camera, editor and brand kit, and checks every take. 10 free demos a month · No card required · Open source, MIT. Works inside the agent you already use: Claude Code, Claude, Cursor, Codex and any MCP client.
- **What your agent can record for you.**
  - **Launch videos:** A polished walkthrough for Product Hunt, your landing page or the announcement post. “Record the new onboarding flow for our launch.”
  - **Changelog clips:** A short clip or GIF for every feature you merge, in the release notes the same day. “Make a GIF of the CSV export for the changelog.”
  - **Help-center guides:** Docs that show the real screen and stay current: run the same prompt again when the UI changes. “Re-record the billing settings guide.”
  - **Sales and onboarding demos:** The exact flow a prospect asked about, without booking a screen share. “Show how a manager approves an invoice.”
  - **Bug reports:** A video of the bug on the issue, so whoever picks it up sees it before reading a line. “Record the steps that reproduce issue #412.”
  - **Social posts:** Short clips for X and LinkedIn, cut tight and in your brand. “Cut a 20-second clip of the new dashboard.”
- **Connected in five minutes.** Pick your agent and paste the commands. Then pair [Toru for Chrome](https://toru.tools/chrome) or [Toru for Mac](https://toru.tools/mac) from the one link your agent sends you.
- **Pay only for demos that pass.** A credit is used only when a video passes the check. [Compare the plans](https://toru.tools/pricing) or [talk to us](mailto:support@toru.tools) about a team.
- **Every line of Toru is yours to read and run.** The recorder, Toru for Chrome, Toru for Mac and the console are public. Self-host it for free with no model key to bring, since your agent does the driving. The hosted plans fund the project and spare you the servers. Source: https://github.com/alifoo/toru
  - **Recorder:** The MCP server your agent talks to: capture, camera, render and the delivery check.
  - **Toru for Chrome:** The extension that records in your own signed-in Chrome.
  - **Toru for Mac:** The app that records, and lets your agent operate, a window on your Mac.
  - **Console:** Demos, connections, brand and billing, the same one we host.
- **Questions before you connect it.**
  - **Is Toru open source?** Yes, under the MIT license. All of Toru is public at https://github.com/alifoo/toru: the recorder, the Chrome extension, the Mac app and the console. Run it yourself, with no model key to bring, or let us run it for you.
  - **Why pay if Toru is open source?** You don't have to: self-hosting is free, forever. The hosted plans are for teams who would rather ship than operate a recorder: no servers, render workers or storage to run, links that work the moment a video is ready, updates the day they ship, and a person to answer when something breaks. Every paid plan also funds the open-source project.
  - **How is this different from Loom or Screen Studio?** Those tools record you doing the flow. With Toru, your agent does the flow from a prompt; Toru records it, adds the zooms, cursor and your brand, and checks the video before it reaches you. Toru is the infrastructure; your agent is the operator.
  - **Does my agent get my passwords?** No. It sees the product address and the plan. You are already signed in in your own Chrome or on your Mac, and a sign-in page stops the recording instead of being recorded.
  - **What uses a credit?** One delivered video that passed the check. A blank, frozen or too-short take is held back and costs nothing; downloads and technical retries do not use another credit.
  - **Can it record a Mac app?** Yes. Toru for Mac records the window you share and, when you allow it, operates that window for your agent. Same account, same credits.
# Give your agent a camera. (https://toru.tools/docs)
Toru is recording infrastructure for your AI agent. Connect it once, pair the Chrome or Mac it records in, and ask for a demo in your own words. This page is the whole of it.
- **1. Connect your agent.** In Claude Code, Claude, Cursor, Codex or any client that supports remote MCP servers, add a connector with the address `https://mcp.toru.tools/mcp`, then sign in to Toru and approve the connection. In Claude Code you can also install the Toru skill from `alifoo/toru-skills`. This connects your agent to Toru; it does not sign in to your product.
- **2. Choose where Toru records.** Toru records in two places, both already signed in as you. It never asks for a password or a code, and a sign-in page stops the run instead of being recorded.
  - **Web apps: your own Chrome.** Install [Toru for Chrome](https://toru.tools/chrome) and pair it once from a link your agent gives you. Each recording opens your product in a window of its own, signed in with your session, with no click from you. Your cookies and storage never leave Chrome.
  - **Mac apps: Toru for Mac.** Install [Toru for Mac](https://toru.tools/mac) with one line in Terminal, `curl -fsSL https://toru.tools/install.sh | bash` (or `brew install --cask alifoo/toru/toru`), pair it from a link your agent gives you, and choose the window or display to share. You approve what is shared, and you can stop sharing at any time.
- **3. Ask for a demo.** “Record a demo of creating an invoice in https://app.acme.com: open Invoices, click New invoice, choose Acme Inc. as the customer, save, and end on the invoice page.” Before recording, your agent writes a short plan of the flow: the screens, the exact buttons and fields, the values to use and what the last screen should show. If it can read your product’s code it uses that; otherwise it looks at the live product. The more specific your request, the better the demo. Ask for one flow per demo. Then your agent records the flow itself, one click at a time, in a window Toru opens for it. When the last screen is on show it tells Toru it is done; Toru holds on that screen, stops, renders the video with your brand and checks it. Your agent spends a few tokens per step; Toru adds no model of its own.
- **Your brand.** In the console, open **Settings** and paste your product’s address: Toru reads its colour and logo from the site. Adjust the background, padding, intro and outro cards, the camera’s zoom, the cursor, the GIF and the output size, then save. Every demo of that product uses them automatically.
- **Delivery check and credits.** Every video is checked before delivery. Blank, frozen or too-short videos are held back as needing review and never charged; you can record again or accept the video anyway. One credit is used when a video is delivered. See [pricing](https://toru.tools/pricing).
- **Your demos.** Your agent hands you links to the MP4 and GIF. Every demo also stays in Demos for your plan’s storage period, with each step of the plan on the video’s timeline. Changed your brand? Render a demo again from there while its capture is kept; it uses no credit.
- **If something goes wrong.**
  - **Needs review:** the video did not pass the check and no credit was used. Ask your agent to record again with a clearer flow.
  - **Stopped at a sign-in page:** sign in to your product in that Chrome or app, then ask again.
  - **Chrome or Mac offline:** open Chrome or the Toru app; a paired device reconnects by itself.
  - **Waiting for capacity:** the beta records one demo at a time across all accounts. A run that finds Toru busy waits its turn, up to ten minutes, before recording; your agent can keep polling its status.
  - **Anything else:** email [support@toru.tools](mailto:support@toru.tools).
- **Run it yourself.** Toru is open source under the MIT license: the recorder, Toru for Chrome, Toru for Mac and the console are at [github.com/alifoo/toru](https://github.com/alifoo/toru). Run it on your own machines, with no model key to bring: your agent drives. The hosted service is the same code, run for you.
# Toru for Chrome (https://toru.tools/chrome)
Chrome 120 or newer. Record a demo in your own Chrome, where you are already signed in to your product. Your agent asks Toru for the demo; Toru opens the product in a window of its own and records the flow with the same cursor, zooms, brand and delivery check as every Toru video. No sharing dialog, no click per recording.
- **Connect.** Each recording opens a new window on your product. Leave it open until the recording ends; Toru closes it. If the product asks you to sign in, sign in in that window and ask your agent to record again.
  1. Ask your agent to connect Toru for Chrome. It calls `extension_pair` and gives you a one-time link.
  2. Open the link in the Chrome where you installed the extension. It connects by itself; the page says **Chrome connected**.
  3. Ask for a demo. Your agent finds the connected Chrome with `extension_devices` and records with `recording_run`.
- **What the extension can do.** Toru controls only the window it opens for a recording. It starts on the product your agent asked to record and follows the demo wherever it goes, such as a consent screen or a checkout; Chrome shows a notice while it does. It cannot read your other tabs, and it never sends Toru your passwords, cookies or browser storage. A password or one-time-code field stops the recording instead of being recorded. The video of that window is uploaded to Toru to produce your demo. See [privacy details](https://toru.tools/privacy#chrome).
- **Disconnect.** Click the Toru icon in the toolbar and choose **Disconnect this Chrome**, ask your agent to call `extension_disconnect`, or remove the extension in `chrome://extensions`.
# Toru for Mac (https://toru.tools/mac)
macOS 15.0 or newer · Apple silicon. Record one window or one display that you choose, when you approve it. Toru uploads the finished video for rendering and your agent delivers the MP4.
- **Set up.**
  1. Open Connections and click **Pair a Mac**, or ask your agent to call `desktop_recording_pair`. Either gives you a one-time setup link.
  2. Open the link (or paste the code into Toru). Choose a window or display and approve recording and upload.
  3. Click **Share selected source** and tell your agent “ready”, or click **Record now** to record yourself and ask your agent to render it afterwards.
- **What leaves your Mac.** Capture happens locally and is written to `Movies/Toru`. Only after you approve a recording is the finished video uploaded to Toru for rendering and delivery; your agent sees status and the rendered MP4, not your screen in real time. Desktop content is uploaded unredacted: close private windows and notifications before you approve. Recordings are video only, without audio. Toru operates the shared window only if you turn on “Let your agent operate the shared window” in Settings, and then only during recordings your agent requests. Raw captures and MP4s follow your plan’s retention; local copies stay until you delete them or the 30-day rule moves uploaded copies to the Trash. Failure reports to Toru are off unless you enable them and contain only error codes and versions. See [privacy details](https://toru.tools/privacy#mac).
- **Requirements and limits.** macOS 15.0 or newer on Apple silicon, Screen Recording permission, 500 MB free disk space, and a Toru account connected to an MCP client. Recordings are limited to one source and five minutes per capture. Protected content (DRM video, some secure fields) may record as black.
# Pay for demos that pass. (https://toru.tools/pricing)
One credit per delivered demo; a held-back take is never charged. Start free, upgrade when your agent records more.
- **Free:** $0 / month. Try your first workflows. 10 credits per month, up to 2 minutes per capture, 7 days of MP4 storage. No card required.
- **Creator (Recommended):** $19 / month. Record and share regularly. 50 credits per month, up to 5 minutes per capture, 30 days of MP4 storage. Everything you need for regular demos.
- **Studio:** $49 / month. For a larger recording workload. 150 credits per month, up to 5 minutes per capture, 30 days of MP4 storage. 3× the Creator credit allowance.
- A team, a contract or invoices, or help running Toru yourself? [Talk to us](mailto:support@toru.tools). Rather run it yourself? Toru is open source and free to self-host. [See the code](https://github.com/alifoo/toru)
- Prices in USD, billed monthly. One credit is used when the first MP4 from a recording is delivered. Downloads and technical retries do not use another credit. Unused credits do not roll over.
- **Included in every plan:** One-prompt demos · Delivery check before charging · Brand per product · MP4 and GIF · Your Chrome or your Mac · Claude, Cursor, Codex via MCP
- **Before you start:** You need an MCP-compatible agent, such as Claude Code, Claude, Cursor or Codex. Your agent subscription is separate. Toru is in limited public beta; checkout is available after account admission. Cancel renewal in the app. Paid plans include a [14-day refund policy](https://toru.tools/terms#refunds).

# Privacy Policy (https://toru.tools/privacy)
Public beta · effective October 11, 2026. This policy explains how Toru, operated by Alisson Ayres (“we”, “us”), handles personal data when you use the website, the console, the connector your AI agent uses, Toru for Chrome and Toru for Mac. For privacy requests, email [support@toru.tools](mailto:support@toru.tools). See also the [Terms of Service](https://toru.tools/terms).
- **What we collect.**
  - **Account data:** your name, e-mail address and sign-in details, and the connections you authorize for your agents (stored as hashed credentials).
  - **Recording requests:** the product address, the flow and plan your agent sends, field values it provides, and the brand settings you save.
  - **Recording content:** the screens of the product being recorded, page observations used to carry out the flow (such as the page address, visible text and the labels of controls), cursor positions and the steps taken, and the videos and previews we produce. Recorded screens may contain personal data shown by the product.
  - **Paired devices:** identifiers for the Chrome browsers and Macs you pair, with their access tokens stored in hashed form.
  - **Billing:** plan, invoices and payment status. Card details are handled by our payment provider and never reach us.
  - **Usage and diagnostics:** credit usage, request and error logs, and failure reports you choose to send.
  - **Support:** messages and feedback you send us.
- **How we use it.** We use this data to run, recover and deliver your recordings, check videos before delivery, apply your brand, manage accounts, credits and billing, prevent abuse and keep the Service secure, answer support and privacy requests, and meet legal obligations. Our legal bases are performing our contract with you, our legitimate interest in operating and securing the Service, your consent where we ask for it, and legal obligations. We do not sell personal data or recording content, and we do not use it for advertising.
- **Passwords and sign-in.** Your agent never needs your product password and is only shown the product address. Toru records in your own Chrome or on your Mac, where you are already signed in, and never asks for a password or a sign-in code. A sign-in form appearing during a recording stops the recording instead of being recorded.
- **Who processes it.** We share data only with service providers that help us operate Toru, under agreements that limit their use to providing their service to us:
  - an authentication provider, for sign-in and account sessions;
  - cloud hosting and storage providers, for running the Service and storing recordings;
  - a payment processor (Stripe), for checkout, invoices and refunds;
  - AI model providers, which receive page observations from the recording and the instructions your agent sent, to decide the next step of a recording.
  - Your own AI agent and its provider process your prompts and what Toru returns under their own terms. We may disclose data when required by law or to protect rights and safety. A current list of providers is available on request.
- **How long we keep it.** On the Free plan we keep raw captures for up to 24 hours and delivered MP4s for up to 7 days; paid plans keep MP4s for 30 days. You can delete recordings in the console. Account, billing, security and operational records may be kept longer where needed to operate the Service, resolve disputes or meet legal duties. Backups are deleted on their own schedule after data is removed from active systems.
- **Your rights.** Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct, delete, export or restrict the use of your personal data, to object to processing, and to withdraw consent. You can revoke agent connections and request account deletion in the console, or email us. We may need to verify that you own the account. You can also complain to your local data protection authority.
- **Cookies.** We use Vercel Web Analytics to count page views, referrers and clicks on our site; it sets no cookies and does not identify you. We use only cookies needed to keep you signed in and to secure the Service, and store small display preferences in your browser. We do not use advertising or third-party analytics cookies.
- **International transfers.** Our providers may process data in countries other than yours. Where required, we rely on appropriate safeguards for these transfers.
- **Security.** We encrypt data in transit, hash access tokens, limit access to what is needed to run the Service, and keep raw recordings for short periods. No system is perfectly secure; tell us at support@toru.tools if you find a vulnerability.
- **Children.** Toru is not intended for anyone under 18, and we do not knowingly collect their personal data.
- **Toru for Mac.** The Mac app records one window or display that you choose, only after you approve it, and saves the video on your Mac in Movies/Toru. The finished video is uploaded for rendering and delivery when a recording you approved stops, or when you choose Retry upload or Record now. Desktop recordings are not redacted: anything visible in the shared window or display, including notifications, is uploaded as recorded, so close private content first. Local copies stay on your Mac until you delete them. Pairing identifies your Mac to your account and never starts a recording by itself; you can disconnect a Mac in the console or the app. Failure reports are off by default and contain only event names, error codes and app versions.
- **Toru for Chrome.** The Chrome extension lets Toru record in your own browser. For each recording your agent requests, it opens a new window on the requested product and controls only that window until the recording ends, following the demo to the pages it visits; Chrome shows a notice while it does. It does not read or control your other tabs. Your passwords, cookies and browser storage stay in Chrome and are never sent to Toru. During a recording it sends Toru the video of that window, cursor positions, the steps taken and the page observations described above. A password or one-time-code field stops the recording. Pairing stores an access token in the extension and a hashed copy with your account; disconnect from the extension menu, through your agent, or by removing the extension. The extension uses this data only to produce your recordings.
- **Changes.** We will post updates here and notify you of material changes before they apply.
- **Contact.** Privacy requests and questions: [support@toru.tools](mailto:support@toru.tools).
